acceptance_criteria.criterion: On the #/repositories page, each repository's Name column renders as a clickable <a> element.
Clicking a repository name navigates to #/repositories/:id (where :id is the repository's encoded ID).
The inline edit (Edit/Save/Cancel) behaviour on the Name cell continues to work correctly.
The route #/repositories/:id is registered in app.js and correctly invokes renderRepositoryDetail.
The route #/repositories/:id is registered after #/repositories to prevent pattern shadowing.
setRouter is called for the new view before router.start().
The JSDoc route registry comment in app.js includes the new #/repositories/:id route.
Navigating directly to #/repositories/:id via URL bar works correctly.

app.js was already complete from WP-003: route #/repositories/:id registered after #/repositories (no shadowing), setRepositoryDetailRouter(router) called before router.start(), JSDoc registry comment includes the new route.

comments.note: repositories.js: the nameLink href is set once at row-build time and never updated if repo.id changes (impossible with current API, but worth noting). If the ID were ever mutable, the href would go stale. Current implementation is correct for the immutable-ID contract.

repositories.js: the new <a> element uses two classes (repo-name-display and repo-name-link). The repo-name-display class is already relied on by CSS and test selectors. The repo-name-link class follows the pattern used for repo-url-link in the URL cell, which is consistent.

repositories.js: the Enter-key handler on nameInput calls saveBtn.click() rather than triggering the save logic directly. This is a minor coupling to DOM state but is the same pattern used throughout the file (workspace-detail.js also does this). No action required; noting for consistency awareness.

summary: AC1: Verified — name cell contains an <a class='repo-name-display repo-name-link'> element. Unit test passes.

AC2: Verified — href uses encodeURIComponent(repo.id) yielding #/repositories/:encoded-id. Special-character ID (org/repo with spaces) correctly encoded to #/repositories/org%2Frepo%20with%20spaces. Both unit tests pass.

AC3: Verified — inline edit/save/cancel flow fully functional after span→link refactor. Edit hides link/shows input; Cancel restores link; Save updates nameLink.textContent and returns to read mode. All 3 unit tests pass.

AC5: Verified via static analysis — #/repositories registered at line 48, #/repositories/:id at line 51. Correct ordering; no pattern shadowing (exact vs parameterised regex).
AC6: Verified via static analysis — setRepositoryDetailRouter(router) called at line 39, router.start() called at line 81.
AC7: Verified via static analysis — JSDoc comment on lines 8–16 includes '#/repositories/:id → Repository Detail (WP-003)'.

AC8: Verified via static analysis of router.js — _resolve() iterates routes in order, decodeURIComponent applied to extracted param groups (line 147). encodeURIComponent in href + decodeURIComponent in router forms correct round-trip for all special characters.
Regression: 64/64 tests pass across all test files (repositories.test.mjs, repository-detail.test.mjs, repo-status-cells.test.mjs, workspace-detail.test.mjs, project-detail.test.mjs).

Edge cases verified: (1) repo with empty/null name shows '—' gracefully; (2) repo ID with '%' characters is correctly round-tripped without double-encoding; (3) route ordering prevents shadowing; (4) save-failure keeps input visible preserving user's edits.

metrics.test_coverage: AC1–AC3 via unit tests; AC4–AC8 via static analysis of app.js and router.js

comments.note: repositories.js: nameLink.href is set once at row-build time. If repo.id were ever mutable (it is not under the current API contract), the href would go stale. No action needed — documented for awareness.

router.js: trailing slash on a parameterised route (e.g. #/repositories/) produces a 404 because ([^/]+) requires at least one non-slash character. This is documented in the router JSDoc and is the correct behaviour, but any future navigation helpers should guard against appending bare trailing slashes.
repositories.js: on save failure, the input remains visible (user keeps unsaved edits). This is correct UX — explicitly verified as intentional, not a bug.

summary: Reviewed repositories.js (the sole modified source file) line-by-line. The span→link refactor is minimal, targeted, and correct.

Naming conventions are consistent: nameLink mirrors the existing urlLink pattern in the same file. Two-class approach (repo-name-display + repo-name-link) correctly preserves CSS/selector compatibility while adding the new semantic class.
Edit-mode state management is clean: editBtn click hides nameLink, shows nameInput; cancelEditBtn and saveBtn restore the correct visibility states. No leaking intermediate state found.

Save path correctly mutates repo.name and updates nameLink.textContent atomically before switching back to read mode. Error path leaves the input visible — intentional and correct per QA verification.
encodeURIComponent on repo.id at row-build time is the right place; href is a static string set once, which is correct under the immutable-ID contract.
app.js is clean: route ordering (exact before parameterised), setRepositoryDetailRouter before router.start(), and JSDoc registry are all correct.

repositories.test.mjs is well-structured. Tests are isolated (cleanup after each), cover the three acceptance criteria, and include a special-character ID edge case. One minor documentation-forward item noted (see comments).
No blocking issues found. No Fix-Forward changes applied. PASS.

comments.note: repositories.js L69–73: nameLink is constructed with two classes (repo-name-display, repo-name-link). This correctly mirrors the urlLink pattern (repo-url-link) and preserves all existing CSS and test selectors. Pattern is consistent and intentional — no action needed.

repositories.js L162–186: Save handler sets saveBtn.disabled=true before the await, and resets it in the finally block regardless of outcome. This is correct defensive coding that prevents double-submit without risk of permanently disabling the button. Clean.

repositories.js L189–195: Enter-key calls saveBtn.click() and Escape calls cancelEditBtn.click(). This is a DOM-coupling pattern but consistent with workspace-detail.js and eliminates duplicated logic. Acceptable for this codebase's style.
